key_insight: CARM improves response-level off-policy control in LLM RL by masking whole sampled responses using absolute token log-ratios, preventing positive and negative drift from canceling out.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a more reliable sequence-level acceptance rule for post-training LLM systems where rollout and training engines differ, helping stabilize optimization for reasoning and code models.
method: Compute sequence-level mask from the average of absolute token log-ratios rather than signed geometric-mean ratios.
Reject responses when bidirectional probability drift indicates substantial off-policy mismatch, instead of letting cancellations hide it.
Provide a theoretical bound linking accepted responses to both ratio-band violations and mean log-distance beyond the band.
evidence_signal: On math reasoning and code benchmarks, CARM improves mean@16 by up to 3.13 points over geometric-mean masking and raises average pass@1 by 2.88 points over the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Absolute-log masking may be more conservative and could reduce useful updates or require careful tuning of the acceptance threshold to avoid over-masking.
paper_title: CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning
